what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/publish-a-site-at-its-own-address: publish a site's files, name it, attach a domain, let an address go, list the addresses.

payload.label: Publish a site
payload.job: Publish a website's pages and files so it can be given its own address
payload.description: Keeps a site's files (files by path, index.html first, text or data: URLs; or site, the name of a site.json in your files such as copy_a_site leaves) under a new installation in your files, or a new version of one already published (installation). Returns the installation id, how many files and bytes, and a name its page title suggests. Give it an address with name_site or attach_domain. A site that already has an address also gets llms.txt, the list of its pages AI apps read, unless it ships its own.

files.description:
The site's files by path, like {"index.html": "

Hi

"}

site.description: The name of a site.json in your files

installation.description: The site's installation id, as publish_site answered it

stored.description: What this run reads of the person's own things, read by the caller from where the person keeps them (the engine keeps none) and given here: files: {name: text or {base64}} under /, /installations/, as this row's `stored` lists. What is not given is not there.

keep.description: What the run made, for the caller to keep where the person keeps it: rows {id, type, value} (value null removes), settings {label, value}, files {file, base64}. The run itself writes nothing.

payload.label: Name a site
payload.job: Give a published website its own readable address, or rename it so old links still work
payload.description: Gives the site (installation) the address https://<name>.<suffix>/: name, or one made from title. A site renamed keeps its earlier names, which send visitors on to the new one. A name is 3 to 40 lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens; reserved words and code-like names are refused. Your computer hands the address to the forwarder and the site answers there while your computer is on.

installation.description: The site's installation id, as publish_site answered it

suffix.description: The host your site names live under, such as sites.example.com: the site's address is its name before it

title.description: Words to make a name from, like the site's title

stored.description: What this run reads of the person's own things, read by the caller from where the person keeps them (the engine keeps none) and given here: files: {name: text or {base64}} under /installations/, as this row's `stored` lists. What is not given is not there.

keep.description: What the run made, for the caller to keep where the person keeps it: rows {id, type, value} (value null removes), settings {label, value}, files {file, base64}. The run itself writes nothing.

payload.label: Put my own domain on a site
payload.job: Put a domain name I own in front of my published website
payload.description: Makes your own domain (domain, like shop.example.com) show the site (installation). Give your account's address (account, the 64 characters after /a/ in your Trillion address): the TXT record names it, so only you can attach your domain. Give the host your computer answers on (points_at): the address record points at it, and the suffix, proof_label and proof_value_prefix the forwarder's settings name. Returns the two DNS records to add at your domain's DNS host; the address answers once the TXT record is visible.

installation.description: The site's installation id, as publish_site answered it

points_at.description: The host your computer answers on, such as app.example.com: the address record of your domain points at it

suffix.description: The host your site names live under, such as sites.example.com: a domain under it is a site name, not your own domain

proof_label.description: The label of the DNS proof record the forwarder checks, such as _verify-example

proof_value_prefix.description: The start of the DNS proof value the forwarder checks, ending in =, such as account=

payload.label: Let go of a site address
payload.job: Stop a website answering at one of its addresses
payload.description: The site stops answering at host (a name or your own domain), and every earlier name that sent visitors to it goes too. Another account may take a name once it has been let go.

payload.label: My site addresses
payload.job: List the addresses my published websites answer at
payload.description: Every address your sites answer at: each host, its https address, the installation it shows, and for an earlier name the address it sends visitors on to. told says what the forwarder last answered: answering, or refused and why.
